title: Retirement of legacy binary-proto transport and migration to JSON-LD streaming v2
creator: Arjun Mehta
description: Replace the legacy binary-proto transport for streaming responses with the standardized JSON-LD streaming v2 format. This ticket defines the migration requirements, compatibility shim window, rollout timeline, telemetry gates, and client guidance to minimize customer disruption.
background: Historically, several internal and partner clients adopted binary-proto framed transport for low-latency streaming. Binary-proto complicates cross-language client support, blocks observability (telemetry and structured output), and limits our ability to add structured function/tool-calling features. JSON-LD streaming v2 is the unified format used across the platform for rich structured output, progressive validation, and easier SDK adoption.
goals: 1) Announce a clear retirement timeline with migration resources. 2) Provide an automated client adapter (shim) and sample PRs. 3) Ensure rollout has telemetry gates and rollback criteria. 4) Deprecate binary-proto transport after a 16-week compatibility window with opt-in telemetry. 5) Ensure zero-loss of customer data during migration and clear customer communications.
scope_in_scope: - Server-side handlers to emit JSON-LD streaming v2 alongside binary-proto for the compatibility window. - Provide official client adapter libraries for Node/Python/Go. - Telemetry: request-level usage, error rates, and content diffs. - Migration docs, CLI checker, and SDK integration examples.
scope_out_of_scope: - Rewriting third-party partner SDKs (we will provide adapters and PR templates only). - Changes to model output semantics beyond transport/frame encoding. - Simultaneous deprecation of other legacy transports (these will be handled separately).
migration_strategy: Phase A (Dual-write shadow): servers emit both binary-proto and JSON-LD streaming v2 for 8 weeks. Phase B (Opt-in enforcement): default to JSON-LD for new sessions but accept binary-proto if client signals legacy header; collect telemetry for 6 weeks. Phase C (Cutover): disable binary-proto accept header after gates pass; remove support after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Announce deprecation plan, provide timeline and migration guide links.
Week 1-2: Release server changes to produce JSON-LD stream in parallel (feature-flagged).
Week 3-6: Publish official client adapters (node/python/go) and a CLI 'transport-check' tool. Share sample PRs for common client repos.
Week 7-12: Shadow traffic and migrate 30% of internal clients via targeted outreach. Monitor diffs and escalate regressions.
Week 13-18: Opt-in enforcement window; require explicit legacy header to receive binary-proto. Continue support but start disable plan if gates met.
Week 19: Cutover: reject legacy header. Post-cutover: 2-week rollback window if major regressions occur.
Week 21: Fully remove server-side parsing for binary-proto and close compat window.
telemetry_and_gates: Gate 1 (pre-enforcement): JSON-LD emitted without increased server CPU or 99th percentile latency > +10% compared to baseline.
Gate 2 (shadow validation): Content-diff rate (token-level mismatches) < 0.5% across shadowed requests.
Gate 3 (error surface): Streaming connection errors attributable to format < 0.2% and customer-reported regressions < 5 over 30 days.
Gate 4 (post-cutover stability): End-to-end error budget consumption < 10% of monthly SLO over 14 days.
rollback_criteria: If Gate 2 shows content-diff rate > 2% for any major customer after migration attempt.
If client-visible 5xxs increase by > 3x sustained for 1 hour post-cutover.
If critical partner refuses to migrate and experiences customer-facing regressions for > 3 days.
acceptance_criteria: Official migration guide published in Console docs with step-by-step examples for Node/Python/Go.
Client adapters published to npm/pypi/github with MIT license and integration tests passing in CI.
CLI 'rw-transport-check' v1 released to validate a client's behavior and sample diffs.
Server-side dual-write behind feature flag and automated e2e tests validating both streams.
Telemetry dashboards (per-route) showing format usage and diff-rate, with alerting configured for gates.

estimate_notes: Estimate 8 points reflecting engineering integration, SDK publishing, docs, and a lightweight CLI. Does not include large partner migrations which will be scoped separately.
